verdict: 28 Sep 2026 refresh: Anarock Q3 2026 top-line released — top-7 unsold rose ~12% YoY to ~6.31 lakh units, with Bengaluru and MMR leading the supply build-up (Bengaluru city-level Q3 PDF still due early Oct). Q3 sales +3% YoY, +10% QoQ. Bengaluru avg residential prices +8% YoY. RBI holds repo at 5.25% (neutral); next MPC 5–7 Oct 2026. Knight Frank H1 2026 affordability at 35% EMI/income for Bengaluru unchanged; H2 print due Dec. April 2026 Karnataka guidance-value revision still not gazette-notified — remains a red-tilt event whenever it lands. Composite tilt: mildly higher — supply overhang widening while affordability holds within threshold.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.value: Top-7 unsold ~6.31 lakh units (+12% YoY) Q3 2026; Bengaluru leads build-up
indicators.note: Anarock Q3 2026 top-line: pan-India unsold across top-7 cities rose ~12% YoY to ~6,30,590 units (from ~5,61,760). Q3 sales +3% YoY, +10% QoQ — MMR and Bengaluru led the sales momentum but also the supply pile-up. Bengaluru avg residential prices +8% YoY in Q3. Anarock/JLL/Knight Frank/Meraqi Q3 Bengaluru city-level breakdowns due early Oct 2026 — carrying Q2 anchor of Bengaluru unsold +34% YoY and ~6–7 quarters to sell. Overhang still concentrated in East Bengaluru (Whitefield, Sarjapur).

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: Anarock Q2 2026 pan-India breakdown: ₹80L–1.5Cr = 27% of launches, ₹1.5–2.5Cr = 25%, above ₹2.5Cr = 22%. Only ~4% of new supply catered to sub-₹80L buyers — Bengaluru mirrors this skew. Developers continue to pivot to premium as mid-segment demand thins and inventory pressure builds. Q3 2026 breakdown pending early-Oct city release; unchanged since 13 Sep 2026.

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.value: 35% (Knight Frank H1 2026); repo held at 5.25% since 5 Aug
indicators.note: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026: Bengaluru EMI/income at 35% (from 34% in H2 2025) despite ~125 bps cumulative RBI easing. RBI Aug 2026 MPC unanimously held repo at 5.25% with neutral stance; next MPC 5–7 Oct 2026. Typical home-loan rates ~7.25–8.25% (SBI floor 7.25%, HDFC starts 7.75%). H2 2026 Knight Frank release due Dec 2026. Unchanged from 13 Sep 2026.
indicators.src: Knight Frank Affordability Index H1 2026; RBI MPC Aug 2026

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report June 2026: housing-loan GNPA at 0.5%; system GNPA at multi-decade low of 1.8%, projected to rise only to 1.9% by Mar 2028 under baseline. Secured retail GNPA 0.7%; unsecured retail 1.7% flagged for watch as non-housing retail now 58.4% of household borrowing. CRAR 17.7%, CET1 15.3%. Next FSR due Dec 2026. Unchanged from 13 Sep 2026.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.value: Indiranagar asking 50–80% over guidance; Devanahalli/Hoskote 15–25%; April 2026 revision still not gazetted (as of 28 Sep 2026)
indicators.note: Indiranagar guidance ~₹12k/sqft vs asking ₹18–22k/sqft (50–83% premium). Newer corridors (Devanahalli, Hoskote) narrower at 15–25% and partially compressed after the Feb 2026 BBMP guidance hike (6–15%). The statewide 10–15% (up to 30% in select micro-markets) revision proposed 14 April 2026 remains not gazette-notified as of 28 Sep 2026 — sub-registrars still split on which value to apply. Persistent wide gap in prime pockets remains a clear froth signal; gazette landing would be a further red-tilt trigger.

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: Karnataka FY25–26 stamps revenue ~₹20,837 cr (record); Jul/Aug 2026 monthly still not published
indicators.note: Karnataka Stamps & Registration posted a record ~₹20,837 cr in FY25–26 (largely Bengaluru). Headline revenue is inflated by the Aug 2025 fee doubling (1%→2%) and Feb 2026 guidance hike — volume growth softer than revenue growth. IGR Karnataka has not published Jul/Aug/Sep 2026 monthly aggregates as of 28 Sep 2026; keeping figure unchanged pending primary source. Kaveri 3.0 (AI-driven) rollout still flagged for FY26–27.
